context.requirement_text:
Second half of ISS-0431/GH#835's fix for its own stated PRIMARY
surface, atop REQ-216's core module. Mirrors REQ-186/REQ-187's and
REQ-214/REQ-215's own "core module first, wiring requirement(s)
second, disjoint files" split precedent in this file.

TWO ADMISSION GATES, NOT ONE, because tenant identity is not known
until partway through `Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline`'s existing chain --
read in full (lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex): `Plug.Parsers` runs
first, then `assign_trace_id`, then `Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline`
(which itself resolves tenant identity via a DB read -- token
verification, tenant-by-realm/slug resolution, JIT provisioning --
i.e. AuthPipeline's OWN work already consumes a DB connection BEFORE
any tenant identity exists to gate on), then
`Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`, then `match`/`dispatch`. Given that
ordering, a single per-tenant-only gate cannot run early enough to
cover AuthPipeline's own connection use. Resolved as follows, stated
as an accepted, disclosed limitation rather than silently glossed
over (matching this project's own honesty convention for a limitation
that cannot be fully closed within one requirement's scope, e.g.
decision 0014's own disclosed WASM native-crash gap):

1. GLOBAL gate, mounted FIRST in the chain -- before `Plug.Parsers`,
so a request rejected for lack of capacity is rejected before any
body-parsing work is spent on it. Calls
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire(:global)`. Covers AuthPipeline's own
connection use (the gap named above) because it runs before
AuthPipeline and gates ALL downstream DB-connection-holding work,
auth included.
2. PER-TENANT gate, mounted immediately AFTER `Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline`
(tenant identity now resolved into `conn.assigns.auth_context.tenant_id`)
and BEFORE `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`/`match`/`dispatch`. Calls
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire({:tenant, schema_name})`, resolving
`schema_name` the same way `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus` and
`Letflow.Scheduler.Poller` already do (tenant-id -> schema-name
resolution already exists in this codebase; reuse it, do not
re-derive). Covers TenantStatus's own DB lookup and every sub-router's
dispatch work -- the dominant share of connection-holding time per
REQ-056/ISS-0431's own round-trip profiling.
DISCLOSED LIMITATION: AuthPipeline's own DB work (steps 1-4 of its
moduledoc) is covered by the global gate only, not a per-tenant one,
because tenant identity does not exist yet at that point in the
chain. This is accepted, not silently omitted -- state it in this
plug's own moduledoc.
3. Both gates: on `{:error, :capacity}`, respond immediately (halt the
plug chain, no further plugs run) via
`Letflow.Api.Response.service_unavailable/2` (REQ-066, ALREADY
EXISTING -- do not add a new response helper), with the
`Retry-After` header set explicitly on the conn first (matching
`Response.rate_limited/2`'s own documented "caller sets Retry-After"
convention) to a fixed, configured seconds value (config, default 1)
-- NOT a computed estimate, since this admission mechanism has no
queueing/backoff-timing model to estimate from (a fixed short value
matching `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`'s own existing `@retry_after_seconds
"30"` precedent's SHAPE, though the specific number here is
independently justified: admission rejection is a near-instant
decision with no wait queue behind it, unlike TenantStatus's
migration-in-progress case, so a MUCH shorter retry-after is
appropriate -- state this reasoning in the plug's moduledoc rather
than copying TenantStatus's 30-second value uncritically).
4. On success at BOTH gates: the plug stores both `admission_ref()`s
in `conn.assigns` and registers a `Plug.Conn.register_before_send/2`
(or equivalent, matching how this codebase already threads
request-scoped cleanup -- state which mechanism is chosen and why) or
calls `Letflow.Admission.release/1` for both refs when the response is
sent, so an admitted request's slot is freed exactly once, on every
response path including a request that raises inside a downstream
plug or router (verified in the acceptance criteria below).
NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no change to REQ-216's core semaphore logic;
no change to `Letflow.Plugs.RateLimit` (still deferred, unmounted,
unrelated mechanism); no Poller wiring (REQ-218); no tier-weighted
per-tenant caps (REQ-216's own recorded open question).

task.description: CODE-DESIGNER rework, its own numbered step (01e) distinct from the earlier CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR rework cycle (01b-01d), triggered by SECURITY-REVIEWER's step-03 FAIL: a single admitted HTTP request holds TWO units of Letflow.Admission's shared global budget simultaneously for nearly its entire lifetime, because the global gate's ref was held open across the tenant gate's own composing (global+tenant) acquisition instead of being released once AuthPipeline's DB work concluded. Evaluated SECURITY-REVIEWER's suggested fix (release-before-second-acquire) against an alternative (skip the tenant gate's own global-consuming acquisition, reusing the already-held global ref) and chose the former.
acceptance_criteria: design doc states precisely where and how the global gate's ref is released relative to the tenant gate's acquisition, with no ambiguity for ELIXIR-DEV to guess at

design doc explicitly answers whether releasing the global gate's ref before the tenant gate acquires creates a race where another request could take the freed slot before this request's tenant-gate acquisition runs, and states whether that is accepted behavior or a defect needing further design

design doc explicitly justifies not changing Letflow.Admission's (REQ-216, already merged) public API, state shape, or atomicity algorithm, or explains why a change would be required if the chosen fix needs one
design doc updates the exact api_pipeline.ex plug chain order to reflect the fix
design doc flags for TEST-DESIGNER that AC3/AC4's minimum-global-cap arithmetic in test/letflow/plugs/admission_pipeline_test.exs must be re-derived (global_cap == 1, not 2) to match the fix
no implementation code (function bodies) introduced in the design doc -- signatures/@spec/prose only

result.summary:
Read SECURITY-REVIEWER's step-03 FAIL in full, the current design doc (lib/letflow/design/req217-http-admission-wiring.md), the shipped implementation (lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex, lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex), and REQ-216's own design doc's §0 decisions (composing rule, atomicity algorithm, opaque admission_ref() type) to confirm REQ-216 imposes no obligation to accommodate a caller holding one ref across two dependent gates.

Added a new §10 to lib/letflow/design/req217-http-admission-wiring.md (after the existing §9, renumbering nothing else) specifying the chosen fix:

CHOSEN FIX (SECURITY-REVIEWER's suggested direction, adopted as-is): release the global gate's ref immediately after Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline completes, via a NEW plug (a new public Letflow.Plugs.Admission.release_global_ref(conn) function, mounted through a thin local wrapper the same way :assign_trace_id already is) inserted between AuthPipeline and the existing pool: :tenant Admission mount. The tenant gate's own try_acquire({:tenant, schema}) call is UNCHANGED -- still the full composing (global+tenant) pair in one atomic REQ-216 call -- it is simply now the FIRST global unit held at that point, not a second one stacked on an already-held first. Zero changes to Letflow.Admission's public API, state shape, or atomicity algorithm. New chain order: global Admission mount -> Plug.Parsers -> assign_trace_id -> AuthPipeline -> NEW release_global_admission -> tenant Admission mount -> TenantStatus -> match -> dispatch. Every other release path (auth failure halt before reaching the new plug, a raise before reaching it) is unchanged and still handled by the existing Mechanism A (before_send)/Mechanism B (pdict + handle_errors) exactly as before, since the tenant gate is never reached on those paths and no double-consumption exists there to fix.

ALTERNATIVE REJECTED (§10.2): skipping the tenant gate's own global-consuming acquisition and reusing the already-held global ref. Rejected because it requires either a new Letflow.Admission acquisition shape that opts out of the global co-check (breaking REQ-216's core atomicity algorithm's 'always check both conditions fresh together' guarantee) or passing the already-held opaque admission_ref() into try_acquire/2 for 'transfer' recognition (a new public API surface REQ-216's admission_ref() type -- documented opaque, uninspectable -- does not support). Either variant changes REQ-216's already-merged, already-released public contract to accommodate REQ-217's own composition bug, which the task brief instructs to avoid when a plug-level fix exists (it does).

RACE-CONDITION ANSWER (§10.3, task brief question (a)): yes, a gap exists between the global ref's release and the tenant gate's fresh acquisition, during which another request's try_acquire/2 could win the freed global slot first (Letflow.Admission's single-GenServer mailbox serializes all callers with no priority/reservation carried over from an earlier grant). Consequence: a request admitted at the global gate is NOT guaranteed admission at the tenant gate -- it can be told 'yes' at the first gate and then {:error, :capacity} at the second, after already paying for Plug.Parsers/trace-id/the full AuthPipeline DB round trip. EXPLICITLY RULED: this is accepted, ordinary admission-control behavior, not a defect -- justified on three grounds stated in the design: (1) Letflow.Admission's own moduledoc already documents 'no wait queue... never parked' for every try_acquire/2 call; two calls from the same request were never specially linked by REQ-216's design, only accidentally coupled by REQ-217's original (buggy) ref-holding, which is exactly the mechanism causing the defect being fixed -- removing it necessarily removes the undocumented reservation side effect too; (2) it makes the global counter track ACTUAL DB-connection-holding time more accurately than the buggy version did (this request holds no DB connection between AuthPipeline completing and the tenant gate's own DB use starting, so releasing at that point is correct, not merely convenient); (3) no starvation risk beyond ordinary admission control's own -- the freed slot goes to whichever caller's message is next in the single mailbox, with this request not deprioritized relative to any other. A moduledoc obligation was added (§10.3, extending §8) requiring Letflow.Plugs.Admission's moduledoc to state this re-checked-not-reserved property explicitly so a future maintainer does not 're-fix' it by reintroducing overlap.

Also added §10.4 flagging for TEST-DESIGNER that admission_pipeline_test.exs's AC3/AC4 global_cap == 2 minimum must be re-derived to global_cap == 1 under this fix, since no instant now has an admitted request holding more than one global unit.

Verified no implementation code was introduced: only two @spec-only code fences exist in the doc (both pre-existing, from the original design), and the new §10 describes the new release_global_ref/1 function and the release_global_admission/2 wrapper entirely in prose (function name, arity, delegation target, mount mechanism) rather than as literal Elixir syntax -- matching this doc's own established convention after two prior CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR rework cycles specifically targeted literal-code leakage.
